item.title: Foundation Future cuts health benefits after missing payroll
item.description: Robotics startup Foundation Future ends employee health coverage amid cash crisis after October payroll miss, CEO blames delayed South Korean funding
item.content:encoded:
Foundation Future, a robotic soldier startup led by Indian-origin CEO Sankaet Pathak and backed by Eric Trump, has terminated employee health benefits after missing October payroll. The company cites cash-flow issues from delayed funding by South Korean investor Base Group and will offer COBRA coverage.

  • Foundation Future missed October payroll
  • Health benefits terminated for employees
  • COBRA coverage will be offered
  • CEO blames delayed Base Group funding
  • Startup backed by Eric Trump

Source: Mint

item.title: India take two wickets before lunch on day five against New Zealand
item.description: Washington Sundar and Prasidh Krishna struck before lunch on day five as New Zealand reached 157 for four in the first Test against India.
item.content:encoded:
On day five of the first Test between India and New Zealand, Washington Sundar and Prasidh Krishna took two wickets before lunch. The wickets removed the two New Zealand batters who had been unbeaten overnight, and New Zealand went to lunch at 157 for four, with India's victory hopes still alive.

  • New Zealand went to lunch on day five at 157 for four in the first Test.
  • Washington Sundar and Prasidh Krishna were the two wicket-takers before lunch.
  • The two wickets removed New Zealand's overnight unbeaten batters.
  • India's victory hopes stayed alive with the two strikes.

Source: The Hindu

West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya has called for protests over alleged attacks on Hindus in Bangladesh. He claims Bangladesh was created on religious grounds, not linguistic ones, and says Bengali-speaking Hindus are now facing persecution as a consequence of Partition.

  • Samik Bhattacharya calls for protests over attacks on Hindus in Bangladesh

  • Says Bengali-speaking Hindus face persecution due to Partition

item.title: Paolo Bulgari, former Bvlgari chairman, dies at 89
item.description: Paolo Bulgari, the third-generation businessman and former Bvlgari chairman who drove the brand's global expansion, has died at 89.
item.content:encoded:
Paolo Bulgari, a third-generation member of the family behind the Italian luxury jewellery house Bvlgari, has died at the age of 89. As a former chairman of the company, he oversaw its expansion worldwide and its diversification into watches, perfumes and hotels.

  • Paolo Bulgari, former chairman of the luxury house Bvlgari, died at the age of 89.
  • He was a third-generation member of the family behind the Italian jewellery business.
  • He helped turn the family firm into one of the world's most prestigious luxury brands.
  • Under his leadership, the company expanded globally and moved into watches, perfumes and hotels.

Source: Mint

item.title: Fined $811m, migrant bail scammers kept operating
item.description: Fraudsters fined $811m for conning detained migrants continued their bail scams and evaded shutdown efforts, leaving migrants behind bars, the BBC reports.
item.content:encoded:
A group of fraudsters who ran a bail business targeting detained immigrants was fined $811 million, but their scams did not stop. According to the BBC, they made millions from people in detention, evaded attempts to shut the business down, and left migrants behind bars.

  • Convicted fraudsters were fined $811m for conning detained migrants through a bail business.
  • The BBC reports that the scams continued after the fine was imposed.
  • The operators made millions from detained immigrants, according to the report.
  • They evaded efforts to shut down their bail business.
  • Migrants were left behind bars.

Source: BBC News

item.title: Cyclone Akvan weakens, set to hit Odisha-Andhra coast today
item.description: Cyclone Akvan weakened to a cyclonic storm and is expected to cross the Odisha-Andhra Pradesh coast on Friday, moving at 21 kmph over the Bay of Bengal.
item.content:encoded:
Cyclone Akvan has weakened into a cyclonic storm and is likely to make landfall along the Odisha-Andhra Pradesh coast on Friday. The India Meteorological Department reported the storm moving north-northwest at 21 kmph, centered over the west-central Bay of Bengal at 2:30 am.

  • Cyclone Akvan weakened to cyclonic storm status
  • Expected to cross Odisha-Andhra coast on Friday
  • Moving north-northwest at 21 kmph over six hours
  • Centered over west-central Bay of Bengal at 2:30 am

Source: NDTV

  • Bhat is reported to be trapped in Jammu and Kashmir.
